title: search_logged_models filter string: uppercase the comparison operator before validation so lowercase like/ilike/in/not in are accepted on SQL stores
answers: search_logged_models rejects my filter with 'Invalid comparison operator ... like' when I use lowercase like on the SQL backend
Why does a lowercase 'in' or 'ilike' filter on logged models fail while the same filter works for runs?
Where does parse_filter_string validate the comparison operator for logged model search?
How do I add a new operator or entity type to the logged model filter parser without breaking case handling?
body:
Path: Parses the filter string a user passes to search_logged_models (attribute, param and tag comparisons such as name, params.*, tags.* with =, !=, LIKE, ILIKE, IN, NOT IN) into Comparison objects; the chokepoint is mlflow/utils/search_logged_model_utils.py:parse_filter_string, which splits each statement into identifier, operator and value tokens.
Rule: Normalize the operator to uppercase (op = op.upper()) immediately after the three tokens are split and before Entity.validate_op and SearchUtils.get_sql_comparison_func see it. SQL keywords are case-insensitive, and search_runs and the file store already uppercase the operator, so the SQL logged-model path must match.
Symptom: On a SQL backend, a user writing `name like 'model-%'`, `name ilike ...` or `name in (...)` got 'Invalid comparison operator for attributes.name: 'like'. Expected one of ('=', '!=', 'LIKE', 'ILIKE', 'IN', 'NOT IN')', while the uppercase form worked. Lowercase `not in` already worked only because _join_in_comparison_tokens rewrites it to 'NOT IN' earlier.
Constraints: Applies to operator tokens in logged model filter strings for SQL stores. Do not add per-operator lowercase checks elsewhere; the single uppercase step covers attributes, params and tags. The value side is not changed by this rule.
applies: Logged model search filter parsing (search_logged_models) on SQL backend stores; not the runs search grammar, which already uppercases operators.
says: Searching logged models with lowercase comparison keywords like 'like' or 'in' fails with an error.
Model search filter queries reject lowercase operators that work normally in run searches.
Allow case-insensitive operators when filtering logged models by name, parameters, or tags.
Filtering models on SQL databases should accept lowercase pattern matching and membership conditions.
Invalid comparison operator error appears when searching models unless keywords are capitalized.
search: In logged model search filter parsing on SQL backends, parse_filter_string in mlflow/utils/search_logged_model_utils.py must uppercase comparison operators immediately after token splitting. Normalizing operators with op.upper() before Entity.validate_op and SearchUtils.get_sql_comparison_func aligns SQL logged-model search with search_runs by accepting lowercase operators such as like, ilike, in, and not in. This single normalization step handles attribute, param, and tag comparisons without needing per-operator lowercase checks elsewhere. This rule applies strictly to operator tokens in logged model filter strings for SQL stores, leaving comparison values and the runs search grammar unchanged.
